chapter: Philadelphia, Detroit and back to Atlantic City
title: Other Atlantic City performers: Grace Jackson, Mary Stafford, Mattie Hite
summary: He names Billy Leadman, the dancer Grace Jackson, and singers Mary Stafford, Mattie Hite and Bee Palmer.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I always remember that Frankie Jackson was nice. He was from Chicago. He was a nice guy. And another guy from Chicago, Billy Leadman. He was very good. And then they had a woman there. Nobody's ever danced like she, since. Was Grace Jackson. Grace Jackson was a terrific dancer, but she got up with one of those pimps around there and he got her on dope, see?

And then we had such singers as Mary Stafford, worked with Madison Reed and with Eubie Blake. She was one of the greatest. You could hear her four or five blocks away, yelling, when she would sing. I knew her as a kid, as I told you, I used stare and look in the window for her. And I had the nerve to fall in love with her when I was a kid. You see?
And she looked at me and said, 'Get out of the way, you little bugger.'

So, and then there was a woman there called Mabel -- what was her name, Mabel, I can't think of it -- and then we had the great Mattie HITE, was there. There was a woman called A Bee Palmer. These were great singers. These were all great singers.
